findings.F1: The book earns almost all of its gain on one bar, the Friday-close bar held into Saturday, and most of that gain is timing rather than the market's rise. The mean per-bar position gain is 0.2671 % on Friday bars, 0.0836 % on Saturday bars and between −0.009 % and +0.006 % on every other weekday. The market's own rise accounts for only 0.0098 % of the 0.0483 % mean gain per bar.
findings.F2: The idea is present in the data, but as a jump at the top rather than a straight line. Fridays sorted into quintiles by the 14-day rise in usual moves give 2-day returns of −0.14 %, −0.26 %, +0.55 %, +0.66 % and +1.81 % (top quintile t 6.2, about 409 cases each). That shape fits the plan's linear slope test on the self-standardised forecast poorly, which gave slope t 1.29. The forecast terciles still rise in order: +0.78 %, +1.12 %, +1.44 %.
findings.F3: The weekend effect sits almost entirely in the Saturday leg. After a 14-day rise, Saturday returns +0.90 % and Sunday +0.27 %; after a 14-day fall, Saturday returns −0.11 % and Sunday +0.04 %. The next-day return after a rise minus after a fall has Welch t 5.85 on Friday closes and at most 1.70 on any other weekday's close.
findings.F4: The same rise measured at Thursday's close also shows up on Saturday. After a rise, the Saturday leg is +0.69 % against +0.13 % after a fall, and the Friday leg is +0.39 % against +0.16 %.
findings.F5: The 14-day lookback is the strongest of those tried for the Friday-to-Sunday move. Top-tercile minus bottom-tercile Welch t is 1.91 for 3 days, 2.02 for 7, 5.34 for 14, 4.15 for 28 and 1.43 for 56 days.
findings.F6: Measured as an excess over each coin's 2-day mean, the effect is sure. Friday cases with a 14-day rise beat that mean by +0.91 % per case, with t 3.35 when the cases of each day are summed (265 days).
findings.F7: The gain is not one coin or a few trades, but it is uneven across years.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 14-day rise, measured in its usual daily moves at Friday's close (UTC), the more it rises over the following Saturday, the next 24 hours.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold a coin long for the Saturday after a two-week rise, holding it more firmly the larger the rise, and would leave the Sunday out because it adds little.
ideas.name: two-week rise lifts Saturday

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 14-day rise, measured in its usual daily moves at Thursday's close (UTC), the more it rises over the following Saturday.
ideas.consequence: A trader would read a two-week rise already on Thursday as a reason to expect a stronger Saturday, and could position ahead of the Friday close.
ideas.name: Thursday rise foreshadows Saturday

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 28-day rise, measured in its usual daily moves at Friday's close (UTC), the more it rises over the following Saturday and Sunday together.
ideas.consequence: A trader would treat a four-week rise as a second, slower reason to hold a coin long into the weekend.
ideas.name: four-week rise carries weekend
